title: [Advisory] SonicWall SMA1000: unauthenticated SSRF (CVE-2026-102255)
content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation allows remote unauthenticated attackers to make the appliance issue requests to internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations, while separate post-authentication flaws enable full remote code execution on the appliance.
- **Current exploitation status**: UNKNOWN (vendor reports no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation)

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- SonicWall Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 Series appliances (models 6210, 7210, 8200v)
- SSL-VPN running on SonicWall Firewall products are not affected by this vulnerability.
- For specific versions, please check the references.

- **Prerequisites:**
    - CVE-2026-102255: network access to the Work Place interface; no authentication needed
    - CVE-2026-102256, CVE-2026-102257 and CVE-2026-102258: authenticated administrator access
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor platform-hotfixes are available 

##### CVEs IN THIS ADVISORY:
- CVE-2026-102255 CVSS3.0: 10.0 (CRITICAL) - Pre-auth SSRF via unintended forward-proxy in the Work Place interface
- CVE-2026-102256 CVSS3.0: 7.8 (HIGH) - Post-auth OS command injection leading to RCE
- CVE-2026-102257 CVSS3.0: 7.2 (HIGH) - Post-auth Zip Slip path traversal in the AMC leading to RCE
- CVE-2026-102258 CVSS3.0: 5.5 (MEDIUM) - Post-auth stored XSS in the AMC

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://psirt.global.sonicwall.com/vuln-detail/SNWLID-2026-0017


*Timestamp of the Information: 07.10.2026, 07:38*

**Update 12.10.26** 
- **Current exploitation status**: Actively exploited     
- Cybersercurity firm Defused observed exploitation attempts against their honeypots since oct. 8th 2026   https://x.com/DefusedCyber/status/2108543042693058984    
- Cybersercurity firm Previdian recorded exploitation attempts against their honeypots since oct. 9th 2026:  https://previdian.com/CVE-2026-102255
summary: SonicWall has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities in its Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 Series appliances. The most severe is a critical pre-authentication Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) flaw in the Work Place interface, allowing unauthenticated attackers to abuse the appliance as a proxy to reach internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations. Further flaws allow authenticated users with High privileges to achieve remote code execution through OS command injection and Zip Slip path traversal, and to store malicious JavaScript in the management console.
